classification.difficultyReason: Prove a three-term logarithmic identity by expanding quotients and cancelling terms.

content.prompt:
Let $a>0$, $a\ne1$, and $x,y,z>0$. Prove that
$$\log_a\left(\frac{xy}{z}\right)+\log_a\left(\frac{yz}{x}\right)+\log_a\left(\frac{zx}{y}\right)=\log_a x+\log_a y+\log_a z.$$

answer.short: The identity holds: expanding each quotient using the logarithm laws and collecting terms gives $\log_a x+\log_a y+\log_a z$.
answer.worked:
By the product and quotient laws,
$$\begin{align*}
\log_a\left(\frac{xy}{z}\right)&=\log_a x+\log_a y-\log_a z,\\
\log_a\left(\frac{yz}{x}\right)&=\log_a y+\log_a z-\log_a x,\\
\log_a\left(\frac{zx}{y}\right)&=\log_a z+\log_a x-\log_a y.
\end{align*}$$
Adding these equations and collecting like terms gives
$$\begin{align*}
\log_a\left(\frac{xy}{z}\right)+\log_a\left(\frac{yz}{x}\right)+\log_a\left(\frac{zx}{y}\right)&=\log_a x+\log_a y+\log_a z.
\end{align*}$$
